verdict.rationale: Apple's tech-spec page gives some hard numbers: core counts (16-core CPU, 40-core GPU), 546GB/s memory bandwidth, Thunderbolt 5 at 120Gb/s, and external-display limits. However, the AI performance claims are adjectives ('blazing speed') or relative multipliers ('over 3x faster than M1 Max', 'up to 1.8x faster than M1') with no stated test conditions. Missing for 10: CPU/GPU clock speeds, power/TDP figures, a published Neural Engine TOPS number, memory capacity/type support details, and documented test conditions behind the performance claims.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can comparison-shop from a real spec sheet — the vendor publishes clocks, power, memory support, and AI TOPS with test conditions, instead of marketing adjectives

citations.quote: M4 Max with 16-core CPU and 40-core GPU (546GB/s memory bandwidth)
Up to three external displays with 6K resolution at 60Hz over Thunderbolt and one external display with up to 4K resolution at 144Hz over HDMI
Three Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) ports with support for: Charging, DisplayPort, Thunderbolt 5 (up to 120Gb/s), USB 4 (up to 120Gb/s)
